content.goal: Enable a wrist-worn tremor monitoring device by capturing hand tremor motion data for later analysis while confirming required runtime, measurement bandwidth, sampling, and calibration/form-factor needs before component selection.
content.problemStatement: The initial wearable tremor monitor must start with a functional architecture, but key runtime, tremor frequency range, sampling rate, and wearable form-factor/calibration constraints are not yet confirmed. The prototype must not encode component-level choices prematurely.
content.intendedContext: An early-stage team will prototype the wearable device, run short user sessions, and review timestamped motion data exports to decide next embedded component steps.
scope: Functional specification for motion sensing, timing, timestamped data storage, and analysis-ready export.
Functional design for acknowledging wearable comfort constraints and privacy-sensitive handling considerations as non-medical information.
Explicit identification of unknown measurement-bandwidth, sampling, and runtime requirements.
outOfScope: Component-part selection (specific sensor modules, MCUs, boards).
Firmware libraries, PCB layout, schematic validation, and simulation execution.
Medical-device approval, clinical claims, and regulatory certification.
successCriteria: All produced artifacts conform to the v1 contracts.
Explicit and inferred requirements are distinguishable.
Unsupported assumptions are not presented as facts.
The Next Action is derived from concrete blockers and open questions about wearable motion measurement needs.

assumptions.statement: A single short session with a wrist-worn device is sufficient to collect preliminary motion data while runtime and sampling unknowns are still open.
The initial architecture can treat measurement bandwidth, sampling rate, and calibration approach as configurable placeholders until the user confirms targets.
